claims.text: This trip's own telemetry establishes a route deviation. Under POL-RD-01 the governing distance is the trace, not the rounded trip-record copy: gps_trace.trace_distance_km controls where it differs from trip_record.actual_distance_km, and the trace measures 13.52 km against a booked optimal of 10.4 km. The excess is 3.12 km — 30.0% of optimal — and both establishment tests pass (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED.

The rider carries the POL-RD-08 initial burden and has discharged it. The trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all describe the same trip — trip_id TRP-02812 appears on each, and the 10:18:39 start is consistent across the record — and the excess is read from a trace that is unimpaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c): 107 fixes, 100.0% coverage, no gaps, maximum gap 0.0 s and a 10 s sampling interval. No independent corroboration is required on an unimpaired trace, and the burden shifts to the driver.

Nothing on the rider's own record triggers the extra corroboration step in POL-RD-08. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the clause's condition that adds a beyond-trace corroboration requirement for a serial claimant (4 or more claims with 1 or fewer substantiated) does not attach, and the claim stands on the trace as measured.

The driver's only exculpatory route is POL-RD-04, and it exonerates the deviation only 'to the extent' it is attributable to the rider's instruction — the excess between the vehicle leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor for the Paya Lebar Square stop, and nothing more. The chat message is a request for a quick stop ('need to grab something'), and the only derived waypoint fact in the bundle is that the nearest fix passed 35.99 m from the waypoint; no artifact quantifies how many of the 3.12 excess kilometres that one stop added. Under POL-RD-08 the driver must point to a specific artifact to invoke the clause, and no artifact fixes the exonerated distance, so the balance of the measured excess is unexonerated and stands.

To the extent the excess is not exonerated, the refund is arithmetic and not discretionary. On this METERED fare, run against the booked optimal route: recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 10.4 + 0.28 x 14.0) x the fare_breakdown surge multiplier of 1.0, plus the 0.80 platform fee, = 16.32; charged_total is 19.69; so the refund is 3.37, rounded up to SGD 3.40. That is a PARTIAL_REFUND — well under the 90% of charged_total that would require FULL_REFUND.

No advisory covers this trip window. EV-ADVIS-02812-01 is a MISSING artifact carrying weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so its absence is itself citable, and I disclose that it can carry no fact. An external traffic cause — a queue, a breakdown or a closure — cannot be established on this record, and under POL-RD-13 any such assertion is tested against the traffic_advisory and nothing else, so no POL-RD-03 exoneration is available to reduce the measured excess or to supply an amended optimal route.

claims.text: The detour was rider-requested. Chat message MSG-02812-001 is sent by the RIDER at 10:19:39 and reads 'can we stop at Paya Lebar Square first, need to grab something' — an instruction that comes from the rider and names a specific, actionable place, satisfying POL-RD-04(a) and (c). The rider's own claim accepts the stop was asked for ('I only asked for a quick stop').

The instruction is timely under POL-RD-04(b). The meter started at 10:18:39 and the message is timestamped 10:19:39, sixty seconds later — either before the vehicle left the optimal corridor or, at worst, within the three-minute window that limb allows.

The gps_trace corroborates the instruction, so the corroboration test in POL-RD-04 is met: the waypoint_hint resolved from the message (1.381532, 103.831811) is passed at a nearest-fix distance of 35.99 m, far inside the 200 m threshold, at fix index 54. Because the trace does corroborate the instruction, this is not the uncorroborated-instruction case in POL-RD-14 and no contradiction under POL-RD-10(7) arises.

The distance POL-RD-04 excludes is the out-of-corridor run to the requested stop and back. The trace measures 13.52 km against a booked optimal of 10.4 km — an excess of 3.12 km (30.0%) — and the only off-corridor excursion on the record is the single requested waypoint, passed once, at fix 54. There is no off-route ERP gantry, no second waypoint hinted in the chat, and no pickup or dropoff amendment on the trip record to suggest any other detour, so the whole measured excess is attributable to the rider's instruction.

With the rider-attributable excess excluded before the threshold is applied, no deviation survives POL-RD-01, and POL-RD-02 — which runs only where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01 and no exculpatory clause fully excuses it — is never reached. The outcome is NO_ACTION, which under POL-GEN-03 is party-relative: on this rider-filed dispute it leaves fare_breakdown.payment_status of CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd of 0.00 exactly as they stand, so nothing is refunded to the rider and nothing is taken back from the driver.

The driver has discharged the burden POL-RD-08 places on him once the rider shows an excess: he points to a specific artifact (EV-CHAT-02812) and a specific clause (POL-RD-04) that exonerates the detour, rather than a general assertion that the traffic was bad. The uncited-assertion rule in POL-RD-08 is therefore not engaged against him.

No pass-through correction is owed to the rider. The fare breakdown carries no ERP or toll lines at all (on-route, off-route and total all 0.00) and no airport surcharge, and POL-RD-09(3) provides independently that where the detour was rider-caused under POL-RD-04 no ERP refund is due.

There is no repeat-deviation pattern that could uplift the remedy against the driver. The measured excess is 30.0% of optimal and 3.12 km, so on no view is the deviation MATERIAL under POL-RD-01 (neither above 50% nor above 8.0 km), and POL-RD-06 is not triggered at all; in any event driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 368, a ratio of 0 against the 0.05 gate, and POL-GEN-01 confines this test to exactly those two fields.

ruling.explanation:
Both of you: this is a route-deviation dispute on trip TRP-02812 (RydeX, metered). The telemetry is clean — 107 fixes, 100% coverage, no gaps, 10-second sampling, so no POL-RD-07(a)–(c) impairment — and it measures 13.52 km against a booked optimal route of 10.4 km. That is an excess of 3.12 km, or 30.0% of optimal, so both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass (above 20% and above 0.8 km) and a deviation is established on this trip's trace alone. The rider's claim that the trace establishes a deviation is accepted, and the trace figure, not the rounded trip-record copy of 13.5 km, governs.

The driver nonetheless has a complete answer under POL-RD-04. Chat message MSG-02812-001, sent by the rider at 10:19:39 — about a minute after the meter started at 10:18:39 and well before the waypoint was reached at 10:27:39 — reads 'can we stop at Paya Lebar Square first, need to grab something'. It comes from the rider, it is timely, and it names a specific, actionable place. The GPS trace corroborates it: the waypoint resolved from chat_message.waypoint_hint (1.381532, 103.831811) is passed within 35.99 m at fix 54, far inside the 200 m test, so this is not the uncorroborated-instruction case in POL-RD-14 and no POL-RD-10(7) contradiction arises. POL-RD-04 therefore applies, and it excludes the excess distance between the vehicle leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor.

On this record that excursion is the whole of the excess. The only off-corridor movement is the single requested waypoint, passed once, with no second waypoint hinted in the chat, no pickup or dropoff amendment on the trip record, and no ERP line in the fare breakdown at all (on-route, off-route and total all 0.00), so there is no other detour the excess could consist of. The requested point sits well off the booked corridor, and the added distance is the natural cost of going there and back. Excluding it leaves no excess meeting POL-RD-01, no deviation survives, and POL-RD-02 — which runs only where a deviation is established — is never reached.

I reject the rider's argument that the driver failed to prove the size of the exonerated stretch. POL-RD-04 requires a corroborated rider instruction, not a separate detour-distance artifact; once the instruction is corroborated, the excursion is excluded by operation of the clause, and the driver discharged his POL-RD-08 burden by pointing to a specific artifact (EV-CHAT-02812) and a specific clause (POL-RD-04). The rider's complaint that they asked only for a 'quick stop, not a tour' does not change where the stop was: the place they named is off the booked route.

The rest of the record changes nothing. EV-ADVIS-02812-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and can carry no fact; POL-RD-13 is not engaged because the driver relies on no external traffic cause, so nothing turns on the absence of an advisory. No POL-RD-06 conduct referral arises: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 368 completed trips in 90 days, so no pattern is established, and the deviation is not MATERIAL in any event. POL-RD-09 corrects nothing — there are no ERP, toll or surcharge lines, and limb (3) bars an ERP refund where the detour is rider-caused. The rider's serial-claimant corroboration step under POL-RD-08 is not triggered (deviation_claims_60d = 0), and the rider's profile fields are not used against anyone.

Result: NO_ACTION. Under POL-GEN-03 this is party-relative — fare_breakdown.payment_status of CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd of 0.00 stand exactly as they are; the rider is not refunded and nothing is taken back from the driver. For completeness, had the deviation survived, POL-RD-02 against the booked optimal would have given charged_total 19.69 less a recomputed_fare of 16.32 = 3.37, rounded up to SGD 3.40; that computation does not run. No clause produces a referral, and the monetary effect of zero is below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold, so nothing is held and the ruling executes on issue.

To the rider and the driver: the trip's own telemetry shows a real difference, but it is the difference the rider asked for, so nothing is refunded and the SGD 19.69 charge stands.

The deviation is established on the numbers. Under POL-RD-01 the governing measurement is the trace figure, not the rounded trip-record copy: EV-GPS-02812 (weight 1.0, unimpaired — 107 fixes, 100.0% coverage, 10 s sampling, no gaps, max gap 0.0 s) measures 13.52 km against the booked optimal of 10.4 km. The excess is 3.12 km, 30.0% of optimal, which passes both establishment tests (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km). The rider therefore discharged the initial POL-RD-08 burden, and trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown (TRP-02812).

That excess is then fully exonerated under POL-RD-04. The chat log EV-CHAT-02812 shows the rider writing at 10:19:39, sixty seconds after the meter started at 10:18:39, 'can we stop at Paya Lebar Square first, need to grab something', and the driver answering 'ok'. That is an instruction from the rider, well inside the three-minute window, naming a specific place. The trace corroborates it on the exact field the clause names: the waypoint resolved from the message (Paya Lebar Square, 1.381532, 103.831811) is passed at a nearest-fix distance of 35.99 m, far inside the 200 m threshold. The only off-corridor excursion on the record is that single requested stop — no other waypoint is hinted in the chat, no ERP gantry is charged, and the trip record carries no pickup or dropoff amendment — and the measured 13.52 km is consistent with the Serangoon → Paya Lebar → Bukit Batok diversion rather than the direct 10.4 km optimal. The excess POL-RD-04 excludes is therefore the whole 3.12 km.

The rider's submission that no artifact 'quantifies' the exonerated distance is not accepted. POL-RD-04's test is the waypoint corroboration, run on chat_message.waypoint_hint against the trace, and it is met; once the requested stop is corroborated and is the only departure from the corridor, the excess attributable to it is excluded before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied. This is not the uncorroborated-instruction case in POL-RD-14, and there is no contradiction of the kind POL-RD-10(7) describes: a request that was made and a route that followed it are consistent.

With the excess excluded, no deviation survives POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 is never reached. The rider's arithmetic refund of SGD 3.40 (charged_total 19.69 less recomputed_fare 16.32 on a booked-optimal recomputation) does not arise, because it presupposes a surviving deviation. No pass-through correction is due either: the fare breakdown carries no ERP or toll lines and no airport surcharge (on-route, off-route and total all 0.00). No driver compensation is due: the distance billed, 13.5 km, falls short of the 13.52 km trace by only 0.02 km, nowhere near the 1.0 km shortfall POL-RD-04 requires.

The missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02812-01 (weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) is noted: nobody asserts an external traffic cause, so there is nothing for it to excuse and its absence does not escalate the case (POL-RD-13). No repeat-deviation pattern arises (driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 368 completed trips 90d), so POL-RD-06 is not engaged and no conduct referral is produced; no charge line lacks a counterpart in the trace or trip record, so no billing-integrity referral is produced either.

Outcome: NO_ACTION. Under POL-GEN-03 the fare_breakdown payment_status of CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd of 0.00 are left exactly as they are — nothing is refunded to the rider and nothing is taken back from the driver. Confidence 0.90, on a cap of 1.0 from EV-CHAT-02812 and EV-GPS-02812, the two artifacts carrying the deciding fact.

Ruling for both parties on trip TRP-02812.

THE DEVIATION IS MEASURED, AND IT IS RIDER-CAUSED. The telemetry establishes a route deviation. Excluded before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied, no deviation survives, and POL-RD-02 — which runs only where a deviation is established and no exculpatory clause fully excuses it — is never reached.

I do not accept the rider's argument that the exonerated distance is unquantified. POL-RD-04's quantified test is the 200 m waypoint comparison, and it passes on the platform's own derived field. It asks me to exclude the excess between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor; with a single corroborated stop and no other cause on the record, that stretch is the measured excess. There is nothing to apportion. Nor is this the POL-RD-10(7) contradiction: POL-RD-14 confines that to a request the trace corroborates only in part, where the attributable excess cannot be separated — here the trace corroborates the stop and the excess is separable.

THE REFUND FIGURE OF SGD 3.40 IS NOT REACHED. That figure is POL-RD-02's arithmetic against the BOOKED optimal (charged_total 19.69 less recomputed_fare 16.32) and assumes no exoneration. No ERP or toll line and no airport surcharge appears in the fare breakdown, and POL-RD-09(3) provides independently that a rider-caused detour under POL-RD-04 draws no ERP refund.
